name: Peg O’Nell

attributes.attribute: a servant who drowned in the Ribble and returns every seven years
the old name carried by the River Ribble

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Peg O'Nell is a being of British folklore tied to the River Ribble in Lancashire. The Ribble once bore the name of the river goddess Belisama, who was honored at its source and on its shores. Some scholars think her worship involved human sacrifice, and they see Peg O'Nell as a leftover of that rite. Peg was a servant girl who drowned in the Ribble. To punish those who failed to rescue her, she returned every seven years to take a new victim. In Ireland a similar seven-year cycle of drowning is told of Aine, a fairy queen of Lough Gur. On Peg's Night, when the rising river reached for a victim, people offered small birds or animals to the river spirit. A headless stone figure at Waddow Hall on the riverbank is said to show Peg, or else the goddess Belisama.

okr.objective: Present Peg O'Nell as a river being of the Ribble in Lancashire.
key_results: Tie Peg O'Nell to the River Ribble and the goddess Belisama
State the seven-year return cycle and its victims
